name: 2026 NBA Finals — Spurs vs Knicks (Best-of-7)
description: Monte Carlo model of the 2026 NBA Finals: San Antonio Spurs vs New York Knicks, best-of-7, series tied 0-0, Game 1 on June 3, 2026. Each game is a weighted coin (Bernoulli) for a Spurs win. Home-court advantage follows the 2-2-1-1-1 venue pattern: Games 1, 2, 5, 7 in San Antonio (Spurs home); Games 3, 4, 6 in New York (Spurs road). Spurs win ~63.9% at home and ~46% on the road (both tunable parameters). First team to 4 wins takes the series; a series_over guard freezes the result once a team reaches 4 wins so the remaining (already-decided) games cannot change the winner, even though the kernel runs all 7 steps. DECISION-SUPPORT ONLY — this is a calibrated scenario model for reasoning about uncertainty, NOT betting advice or a wagering signal.

context.decision_question: How likely are the Spurs to win the 2026 NBA Finals, and how long is the series likely to last?
context.venue_pattern: 2-2-1-1-1: Games 1,2,5,7 at San Antonio; Games 3,4,6 at New York
key_levers: parameters.p_road_win.params.value — Spurs road win probability (most uncertain input; tune to test sensitivity)
context.safety_note: Decision-support model for reasoning under uncertainty. NOT betting advice, NOT a wagering signal, NOT a prediction of any single game. Probabilities are illustrative estimates.

calibration.source: Estimated Spurs single-game win probability when playing at home in San Antonio (Games 1, 2, 5, 7).
calibration.update_method: Beta-Binomial after observing actual home-game outcomes.

calibration.source: Estimated Spurs single-game win probability when playing on the road in New York (Games 3, 4, 6). Most uncertain input — explicitly tunable.
calibration.update_method: Beta-Binomial after observing actual road-game outcomes.

step_logic.expr: 0 if series_decided == 1 else (1 if random() < win_prob else 0)
